Full Title: Dvché de Parma et de Piacenza / chez Pierre Mortier
Creator: Cóvens et Mortier, publisher
Subject: Parma and Piacenza (Duchy) -- Maps -- Early works to 1800 ; Emilia-Romagna (Italy) -- Maps -- Early works to 1800 ; Parma (Italy : Province) -- Maps -- Early works to 1800 ; Piacenza (Italy : Province) -- Maps -- Early works to 1800 ;
Notes: Relief shown pictorially. Includes illustrations as part of decorative title cartouche in the bottom left, scale bar in the top left. This map first appeared in an atlas in 1643, in the Latin and French editions of Joan Blaeu's Theatrum Orbis Terrarum (1640-3, vol. 3), and over the next three decades it reappeared with considerable frequency in around twenty further editions of Blaeu atlases. By the end of the century the plate had entered the stock of Pierre Mortier, who acquired many of Blaeu's old copper plates as supplementary material for his own ever-expanding atlases. Under Mortier, the plate was reworked it into the state preserved here, with a French title instead of the original Latin one, plus the addition of Mortier's imprint at the bottom of the title cartouche; by this time, it had also developed two cracks at the left edge, which are prominent on this impression. After Mortier's death in 1711 the plate used for this map passed with the rest of his stock to his widow, in whose presence it is recorded in an inventory of 1720 (no. 200), and eventually to his son Cornelis Mortier, who, with Johannes Covens, re-founded the family enterprise as Cóvens and Mortier in 1721. As part of this rebranding, Pierre Mortier's signature on this map was itself replaced with that of the new firm, which continued to issue copies of the map for several decades.
